Proximity Becomes a Target List

Iran’s parliament speaker has turned a speculative New York Times theory about dams into a threat against infrastructure near American and Israeli bases.

Mohammad Bagher Ghalibaf argues that if Iranian dams near missile facilities count as dual-use infrastructure, then dams, ports, and power plants near American and Israeli bases should qualify too.

The Times article itself calls the possible link between water projects and concealed missile facilities speculative. The hypothesis rested on overlapping maps. The paper also corrected a caption to say that strikes hit near the Karun-4 Dam, not the dam itself.

Ghalibaf mocks the idea that proximity proves military use, then uses proximity to justify his own threat.

The newspaper has a correction mechanism. A missile launched on the strength of “nearby” does not.

#Iran #CivilianInfrastructure #MediaAccountability
